If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:

The failing test `testLANG_831` checks if the pattern "M E" correctly parses the string "3  Tue". The current bug report explains that FastDateParser (FDP) does not handle white-space properly: unlike SimpleDateFormat (SDP), FDP treats a single white-space in the pattern as matching any number of white-space characters. This means FDP is more permissive in whitespace matching than the official SimpleDateFormat behavior, causing it to parse dates with whitespace formats that SDP would reject.

Inspecting the `FastDateParser.parse(String, ParsePosition)` method shows that it relies on a compiled regex pattern (`parsePattern`) to match the input date string. The regex is built incrementally from "strategies" representing parts of the date/time pattern. The method applies these strategies in order to parse matched groups from the input string into the Calendar.

The `init()` method constructs the `parsePattern` regex by iterating over pattern fields, getting a corresponding Strategy for each field, and letting the strategy add its regex fragment. The full regex pattern is then compiled and used for parsing.

The `getStrategy(String)` method returns the appropriate Strategy for a format field. For example, 'M' (month) uses either `TEXT_MONTH_STRATEGY` or `NUMBER_MONTH_STRATEGY` depending on length, and 'E' (day of week) uses `DAY_OF_WEEK_STRATEGY`.

The whitespace in the pattern is treated as a "CopyQuotedStrategy` which adds the regex for that literal whitespace via `escapeRegex`. The `CopyQuotedStrategy.addRegex` method escapes the whitespace literally in the regex, but the bug report indicates current behavior matches any number of whitespace characters for a single space.

Hence, the likely issue is that the regex fragment generated for the whitespace literal in the pattern is not strict enough — it is matching a variable number of whitespace characters instead of exactly one whitespace character. This causes FDP to accept strings with different whitespace amounts compared to SDP.

Thus, the root cause is the regex construction for literal whitespace characters in the pattern, specifically in `CopyQuotedStrategy.addRegex` or the `escapeRegex` method it calls. Instead of escaping whitespace literally, it probably replaces spaces with something like `\s+`. This leads to FDP parsing strings with more flexible whitespace, contrary to SDP behavior and causing the test to fail.

No other recent bug reports strongly relate to this whitespace handling issue, confirming it is a distinct problem focused on the regex generation for whitespace literals in the FastDateParser pattern parsing process.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
